questions.prompt: Do you like to take pictures of good scenery?

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Photographing Scenery
idioms: a picture is worth a thousand words

questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, yes, I do. I like to take pictures when I see something nice. Honestly, my phone is usually full of them. It's fun to look back on them later.
questions.sampleBand6: Yes, I do enjoy it. Actually, whenever I come across some really beautiful scenery, I try to capture it. I'm not a professional or anything, but I like having a record of places I've been. I think it's a nice hobby, in a way.
questions.sampleBand7: Yes, I am particularly fond of taking pictures of good scenery. I wouldn't say I'm a great photographer, but I find it very relaxing and enjoyable. Beautiful scenery just jumps out at you, and I like to try and capture that. Plus, it's nice to look back on those photos later and remember the experience.
questions.sampleBand8: Definitely! I really enjoy taking pictures of good scenery. I'm not a professional photographer or anything, but I think it's a fantastic way to capture the moment. When I see something particularly striking, like a sunset over the ocean or a snow-capped mountain, I feel compelled to photograph it. It’s a great way to preserve memories, and it's right up my alley.
questions.sampleBand9: Absolutely, I'm a keen amateur photographer, and I'm particularly drawn to capturing beautiful scenery. I think there's something incredibly rewarding about being able to translate the beauty of nature into a photograph. It's not just about recording a scene; it's about trying to capture the feeling, the atmosphere, the light. I often find myself going out of my way to find interesting landscapes, and I think practice makes perfect, so I'm always trying to improve my skills. Plus, it's a wonderful way to de-stress and get away from it all.
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, very much so. Photographing beautiful scenery is something I find deeply satisfying—there's a real challenge in trying to capture the scale, atmosphere, and emotional impact of a landscape within the constraints of a camera frame. I'm particularly drawn to natural scenery: mountain ranges, coastal cliffs, open plains at sunset. What I find most rewarding is when a photograph manages to convey not just what a place looks like, but how it felt to be there—the quality of the light, the sense of space, the mood of the moment. I tend to be quite patient when photographing scenery, waiting for the right light or weather conditions rather than just snapping whatever is in front of me. Some of my most treasured photographs are of landscapes I've encountered while travelling.
questions.uzSampleBand5: Xo'sh, e-e, ha, yoqtiraman. Yaxshi narsa ko'rsam, suratga olishni yoqtiraman. Rostini aytsam, telefonim odatda ularga to'la. Keyinroq ularni eslab ko'rish qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleBand6: Ha, menga yoqadi. Aslida, qachon biror chiroyli manzaraga duch kelsam, uni aks ettirishga harakat qilaman. Men professional emasman, lekin men borgan joylarimning yozuvi bo'lishini xohlayman. Menimcha, bu bir tomondan yaxshi mashg'ulot.
questions.uzSampleBand7: Ha, men yaxshi manzaralarni suratga olishni ayniqsa yaxshi ko'raman. Men o'zimni zo'r fotograf deb ayta olmayman, lekin bu menga juda taskin beradi va zavq bag'ishlaydi. Chiroyli manzaralar shunchaki ko'zga tashlanadi va men buni aks ettirishga harakat qilishni yoqtiraman. Qolaversa, keyinroq o'sha fotosuratlarni eslab ko'rish va o'sha tajribani eslash yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Albatta! Men chiroyli manzaralarni suratga olishni juda yoqtiraman. Men professional fotograf emasman, lekin menimcha, bu lahzani ushlab qolishning ajoyib usuli. Qachon men ayniqsa ajoyib narsani ko'rsam, masalan, okean ustidagi quyosh botishi yoki qor bilan qoplangan tog'ni, men uni suratga olishga majburman. Bu xotiralarni saqlashning ajoyib usuli va bu aynan men xohlagan narsa.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Albatta, men havaskor fotografman va men ayniqsa chiroyli manzaralarni aks ettirishga qiziqaman. Menimcha, tabiat go'zalligini fotosuratga aylantira olishda aql bovar qilmaydigan darajada mukofot bor. Bu shunchaki sahna yozib olish haqida emas; bu his-tuyg'uni, atmosferani, yorug'likni aks ettirishga harakat qilish haqida. Men ko'pincha qiziqarli manzaralarni topish uchun yo'limdan qaytaman va menimcha, mashq ustalikni yaratadi, shuning uchun men doimo o'z mahoratimni oshirishga harakat qilaman. Qolaversa, bu stressdan xalos bo'lish va undan uzoqlashishning ajoyib usuli.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Ha, juda ham. Chiroyli manzaralarni suratga olish men uchun juda yoqimli narsa—kamera ramkasining cheklovlari ichida landshaftning ko'lami, atmosferasi va hissiy ta'sirini aks ettirishga harakat qilishda haqiqiy qiyinchilik bor. Men ayniqsa tabiiy manzaralarga qiziqaman: tog' tizmalari, qirg'oq jarliklari, quyosh botishidagi ochiq tekisliklar. Eng ko'p mukofotlaydigan narsa, fotosurat nafaqat joyning qanday ko'rinishini, balki u erda bo'lish qanday his etilganini ham etkazishga muvaffaq bo'lganda—yorug'lik sifati, makon hissi, lahzaning kayfiyati. Men manzaralarni suratga olayotganda juda sabrli bo'lishga moyilman, shunchaki oldimda turgan narsani suratga olish o'rniga, to'g'ri yorug'lik yoki ob-havo sharoitlarini kutaman. Mening eng qadrdon fotosuratlarim sayohat paytida duch kelgan manzaralarimdir.

questions.prompt: Do you look out the window at the scenery when travelling by bus or car?

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Scenery While Travelling
sentenceStarters: I find looking out the window...
I also find that observing scenery...

questions.sampleBand5: Well, sometimes I do. Um, if the weather is good. But usually I'm on my phone. So, not really. I look at my phone.
questions.sampleBand6: Um, honestly, it depends. If I'm not driving, then yeah, sometimes I look out the window. If it's a long journey, I often listen to music or something, so I'm not always paying attention to the scenery. But if it's pretty, I might.
questions.sampleBand7: Well, it really depends on the journey. If I'm on a bus, especially in a new place, I will take in the scenery. But if I'm driving, or it's a route I know well, I'm probably more focused on other things, like the traffic or listening to the radio. So, it's not something I always do.
questions.sampleBand8: Actually, yes, I do. I find it quite relaxing to zone out and watch the world go by. Especially if I'm a passenger, not the driver, of course! I think people underestimate the value of just switching off and appreciating the views. It's a good way to clear your head, even if it's just for a short time. Plus, you come across interesting things you wouldn't normally see.
questions.sampleBand9: Definitely, I'm a big believer in appreciating the journey, not just the destination. So, I always try to make time to look out the window and admire the scenery. I think it's important to stay connected with the natural world, and even a short bus or car ride can offer opportunities to do that. It helps me to put things in perspective and appreciate the beauty around us, which I think is essential for mental well-being. It's something I actively seek out.
questions.sampleAnswer: Absolutely, it's one of my favourite things about travelling overland. I find looking out the window at passing scenery genuinely meditative—it gives my mind space to wander and reflect in a way that staring at a phone screen simply doesn't. There's something uniquely satisfying about watching the landscape gradually change as you move through different regions—from urban sprawl to farmland to forest to hills. I particularly enjoy long train or bus journeys through unfamiliar territory for this reason. I also find that observing scenery from a moving vehicle gives you a sense of the geography and character of a place that you can't get from a map or photograph. It's a form of passive exploration that I genuinely value.
questions.uzSampleBand5: Xo'sh, ba'zan qilaman. Um, agar ob-havo yaxshi bo'lsa. Lekin odatda telefonimda bo'laman. Shunday ekan, unchalik emas. Telefonimga qarayman.
questions.uzSampleBand6: Um, rostini aytsam, bu vaziyatga bog'liq. Agar mashina haydamayotgan bo'lsam, ha, ba'zan derazadan qarayman. Agar uzoq safar bo'lsa, ko'pincha musiqa yoki shunga o'xshash narsalarni tinglayman, shuning uchun har doim ham manzaraga e'tibor bermayman. Lekin agar chiroyli bo'lsa, qarashim mumkin.
questions.uzSampleBand7: Xo'sh, bu haqiqatan ham sayohatga bog'liq. Agar avtobusda bo'lsam, ayniqsa yangi joyda bo'lsam, manzarani tomosha qilaman. Ammo agar mashina haydayotgan bo'lsam yoki yaxshi biladigan yo'nalish bo'lsa, ehtimol, ko'proq boshqa narsalarga, masalan, tirbandlikka yoki radioga e'tibor qarataman. Shunday ekan, bu men har doim qiladigan narsa emas.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Aslida, ha, qilaman. Men dam olish va dunyoning o'tib ketishini kuzatishni juda yoqtiraman. Ayniqsa, agar men yo'lovchi bo'lsam, albatta, haydovchi emas! O'ylaymanki, odamlar shunchaki o'chirish va manzaralardan bahramand bo'lishning qadrini past baholaydilar. Bu hatto qisqa vaqt bo'lsa ham, boshingizni tozalashning yaxshi usuli. Qolaversa, odatda ko'rmaydigan qiziqarli narsalarga duch kelasiz.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Albatta, men nafaqat manzilga, balki sayohatdan ham zavqlanishga katta ishonaman. Shunday ekan, men har doim derazadan qarash va manzaraga qoyil qolish uchun vaqt ajratishga harakat qilaman. O'ylaymanki, tabiat olami bilan bog'lanishda bo'lish muhim va hatto qisqa avtobus yoki mashinada sayohat qilish ham buni amalga oshirish imkoniyatini berishi mumkin. Bu menga vaziyatga boshqacha nuqtai nazardan qarashga va atrofimizdagi go'zallikni qadrlashga yordam beradi, bu esa ruhiy farovonlik uchun zarur deb o'ylayman. Bu men faol ravishda izlaydigan narsa.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Albatta, bu quruqlikda sayohat qilishdagi eng sevimli narsalarimdan biri. Derazadan o'tib ketayotgan manzaralarga qarashni chinakam meditativ deb bilaman—bu mening ongimga telefon ekraniga tikilib qolishdan ko'ra, sayr qilish va fikr yuritish uchun joy beradi. Turli hududlar bo'ylab harakatlanar ekansiz, landshaftning asta-sekin o'zgarishini kuzatishda o'ziga xos qoniqish bor—shaharning tarqalishidan tortib fermer xo'jaliklaridan o'rmonlargacha va tepaliklargacha. Ayniqsa, notanish hududlar bo'ylab uzoq poyezd yoki avtobusda sayohat qilishni shu sababli yoqtiraman. Shuningdek, harakatlanayotgan transport vositasidan manzaralarni kuzatish sizga xaritalardan yoki fotosuratlardan ololmaydigan joyning geografiyasi va xarakteri haqida tasavvur beradi deb bilaman. Bu men chinakam qadrlaydigan passiv tadqiqot shakli.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer the mountains or the sea?
questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I think I like the sea actually. I went there last year. The mountains are, um, okay, but I prefer the sea. It's, like, more fun, you know? It is very nice.
questions.sampleBand6: Um, that's a good question. Actually, I think I prefer the sea. I mean, the mountains are beautiful and all, but the sea is just more exciting. You can swim, and build sandcastles, things like that. I guess it depends on what you're in the mood for, but yeah, the sea for me.
questions.sampleBand7: Well, honestly, I think I'd have to say the sea. I appreciate the beauty of the mountains, and the peace and quiet, but I find the sea more invigorating. There's something about the vastness of the ocean that I really enjoy. Plus, I love swimming and being by the coast. So, yeah, the sea wins hands down for me.
questions.sampleBand8: That's an interesting question. I think overall, I'd lean towards the mountains. While I appreciate the allure of the sea, and the fresh sea air, I find the mountains offer a different kind of escape. They're incredibly peaceful, and I enjoy hiking and being surrounded by nature. It's a chance to really get away from it all. The sea is great for a short break, but the mountains offer a deeper sense of tranquility and adventure, if you know what I mean. So, yeah, mountains for me.
questions.sampleBand9: That's a great question! To be honest, while both offer unique appeals, I'm definitely more drawn to the mountains. The sea is wonderful for a quick getaway, and I love the sound of the waves, but the mountains offer a sense of serenity and adventure that I find incredibly compelling. The opportunity for hiking, the breathtaking views, and the sheer scale of the landscape – it's all incredibly awe-inspiring. Plus, I find the mountain air so crisp and clean; it's a great way to recharge your batteries. The sea is fun, but the mountains really speak to my soul, if that makes sense.
questions.sampleAnswer: That's a genuinely difficult choice, but if pressed I'd say the mountains. Both environments are awe-inspiring in their own way, but there's something about mountains that I find particularly compelling—the sheer scale, the drama of the terrain, the way they seem to exist on a timescale completely indifferent to human concerns. Standing at altitude with a panoramic view of peaks and valleys gives me a profound sense of perspective that I find deeply restorative. The sea, of course, has its own power—the rhythm of waves, the vastness of the horizon, the sense of connection to something ancient and boundless. But mountains feel more intimate to me in a strange way, perhaps because you can walk through them and feel genuinely immersed in the landscape rather than simply observing it from the edge.

Siz suzishingiz mumkin va qumdan qasrlar qurishingiz mumkin, shunga o'xshash narsalar. Menimcha, bu sizning nimaga kayfiyatingiz bog'liq, lekin ha, men uchun dengiz.

Men tog'larning go'zalligini va tinchligini qadrlayman, lekin dengizni ko'proq tetiklantiruvchi deb bilaman. Okeanning kengligida menga juda yoqadigan nimadir bor. Bundan tashqari, men suzishni va qirg'oqda bo'lishni yaxshi ko'raman. Shunday qilib, ha, dengiz men uchun shubhasiz g'olib.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Bu qiziqarli savol. Menimcha, umuman olganda, tog'larga moyil bo'lardim. Dengizning jozibasini va dengizning toza havosini qadrlasam ham, tog'lar boshqa turdagi qochishni taklif qiladi deb bilaman. Ular juda tinch va men piyoda sayr qilishni va tabiat bilan o'ralgan bo'lishni yaxshi ko'raman. Bu barchasidan uzoqlashish imkoniyati. Dengiz qisqa dam olish uchun ajoyib, lekin tog'lar xotirjamlik va sarguzashtning chuqurroq tuyg'usini beradi, agar men nima demoqchiligimni tushunsangiz. Shunday qilib, ha, men uchun tog'lar.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Bu ajoyib savol! Rostini aytsam, ikkalasi ham o'ziga xos joziba taklif qilsa-da, meni tog'lar ko'proq o'ziga tortadi. Dengiz tezda dam olish uchun ajoyib va ​​men to'lqinlarning ovozini yaxshi ko'raman, lekin tog'lar men uchun juda juda yoqimli bo'lgan xotirjamlik va sarguzasht tuyg'usini beradi. Piyoda sayr qilish imkoniyati, hayratlanarli manzaralar va landshaftning shunchaki miqyosi - bularning barchasi juda hayratga soladi. Bundan tashqari, tog' havosi juda toza va tiniq deb bilaman; bu quvvatingizni tiklash uchun ajoyib usul. Dengiz qiziqarli, lekin tog'lar haqiqatan ham mening ruhim bilan gaplashadi, agar bu mantiqqa to'g'ri kelsa.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Bu haqiqatan ham qiyin tanlov, lekin agar majbur bo'lsam, tog'lar derdim. Ikkala muhit ham o'ziga xos tarzda hayratlanarli, lekin tog'larda meni o'ziga tortadigan nimadir bor - ularning shunchaki miqyosi, landshaftning dramasi, ularning inson tashvishlariga butunlay befarq bo'lgan vaqt shkalasida mavjud bo'lib tuyulishi. Balandlikda turib, cho'qqilar va vodiylarning keng ko'rinishi menga chuqur tiklovchi ta'sir ko'rsatadigan nuqtai nazarni beradi. Albatta, dengizning ham o'z kuchi bor - to'lqinlarning ritmi, ufqning kengligi, qadimiy va cheksiz narsaga aloqadorlik hissi. Ammo tog'lar menga g'alati tarzda yaqinroq tuyuladi, ehtimol siz ular bo'ylab yurishingiz va landshaftga shunchaki chetdan kuzatishdan ko'ra, chinakam botganingizni his qilishingiz mumkinligi sababli.

questions.prompt: What are the most beautiful sights you have seen while travelling?
questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I think the most beautiful sight... I saw was maybe, um, the mountains in Canada. They were, like, very big and, uh, white. It was really nice. I want to go again. The sky was blue.
questions.sampleBand6: I think one of the most beautiful sights I've seen while travelling was definitely the beaches in Thailand. The water was so clear and turquoise, and the sand was incredibly white. It was absolutely stunning, actually. I'd love to go back there someday. It's a great memory.
questions.sampleBand7: Well, one sight that stands out is when I visited the lavender fields in Provence, France. It was just breathtaking. Honestly, the rolling hills covered in purple, with the sun setting behind them... it was like something out of a painting. I'd highly recommend it if you get the chance to go. A truly unforgettable experience.
questions.sampleBand8: That's a good question. Probably the most beautiful sight I've witnessed while travelling was the sunrise over the Angkor Wat temple complex in Cambodia. It was absolutely magical. The way the light caught on the ancient stones, and the reflections in the surrounding pools… it was quite surreal. Plus, the atmosphere, with all the monks chanting, really added to the experience. I'll never forget it.
questions.sampleBand9: That's a tricky one, there have been so many! But if I had to pick, I'd say witnessing the Northern Lights in Iceland was utterly breathtaking. The sky was ablaze with these shimmering curtains of green and purple, dancing across the horizon. It was such a powerful reminder of the sheer force and beauty of nature. It felt almost spiritual, if I'm honest. It’s one of those experiences that puts everything into perspective, and I’d thoroughly recommend it to anyone. It really is a sight to behold.
questions.sampleAnswer: Several come to mind, but one that stands out vividly is seeing the Himalayan range at dawn from a high-altitude viewpoint. The combination of scale, silence, and light was simply overwhelming—snow-covered peaks stretching across the entire horizon, glowing pink and gold as the sun rose. Another sight that left a deep impression was visiting an ancient temple complex surrounded by dense jungle, where centuries-old stone structures were being slowly reclaimed by enormous tree roots. The contrast between human ambition and the patient power of nature was striking. I've also been moved by simpler sights—a perfectly still lake reflecting a forest at sunrise, or a coastal cliff walk with waves crashing far below. What these experiences share is a quality of beauty that feels genuinely humbling.
questions.uzSampleBand5: Xo'sh, e-e, menimcha, eng chiroyli manzarani... men ko'rganim, e-e, Kanadadagi tog'lar bo'lishi mumkin. Ular, juda katta va, e-e, oq edi. Haqiqatan ham yaxshi edi. Yana bormoqchiman. Osmon moviy edi.

Rostini aytsam, binafsha rang bilan qoplangan, quyosh botayotgan tepaliklar... bu xuddi rasmdagidek edi. Agar borish imkoniyatingiz bo'lsa, juda tavsiya qilaman. Haqiqatan ham unutilmas tajriba.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Bu yaxshi savol. Ehtimol, sayohat paytida guvohi bo'lgan eng chiroyli manzara – Kambodjadagi Angkor Vat ibodatxona majmuasi ustidagi quyosh chiqishi edi. Bu mutlaqo sehrli edi. Yorug'likning qadimiy toshlarga tushishi va atrofidagi havzalardagi akslar... bu juda g'ayrioddiy edi. Bundan tashqari, rohiblarning xirgoyi qilishi bilan birga atmosfera, tajribaga yana ham qo'shildi. Men buni hech qachon unutmayman.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Bu murakkab savol, juda ko'p bo'lgan! Lekin tanlashim kerak bo'lsa, Islandiyada Shimoliy chiroqlarga guvoh bo'lish butunlay hayratlanarli edi, deb aytgan bo'lardim. Osmon ufq bo'ylab raqsga tushayotgan yashil va binafsha rangli yaltiroq parda bilan yonardi. Bu tabiatning shunchaki kuch va go'zalligini kuchli eslatma edi. Bu deyarli ma'naviy tuyuldi, rostini aytsam. Bu shunday tajribalardan biriki, hamma narsani o'z o'rniga qo'yadi va men buni hammaga to'liq tavsiya qilaman. Bu haqiqatan ham ko'rishga arziydigan manzara.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Esimga bir nechta narsa keladi, lekin eng yorqin esda qolgani – ertalab, baland tog'li nuqtadan Himolay tog' tizmasini ko'rish bo'lgan. Miqyos, sukunat va yorug'lik kombinatsiyasi shunchaki hayratlanarli edi – quyosh chiqishi bilan pushti va oltin rangga bo'yalgan, butun ufq bo'ylab cho'zilgan qor bilan qoplangan cho'qqilar. Yana bir chuqur taassurot qoldirgan narsa – qalin o'rmon bilan o'ralgan qadimiy ibodatxona majmuasiga tashrif buyurish bo'ldi, u yerda asrlar davomida qurilgan tosh inshootlar asta-sekin ulkan daraxt ildizlari tomonidan qayta egallanar edi. Insoniyat ambitsiyalari va tabiatning sabrli kuchi o'rtasidagi farq hayratlanarli edi. Bundan tashqari, oddiyroq manzaralar ham meni hayajonga soldi – quyosh chiqishida o'rmonni aks ettiruvchi mukammal sokin ko'l yoki pastda to'lqinlar urilayotgan qirg'oq qoyalari bo'ylab sayr qilish. Bu tajribalarning barchasini birlashtirib turadigan xususiyat – o'zini haqiqatan ham kamtar his qiladigan go'zallik sifatidir.

questions.prompt: What did you enjoy doing as a child?
questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I liked to play outside. Yeah, with my friends. We played football, every day. It was fun. I also watched TV. Cartoons were good.
questions.sampleBand6: As a child, I spent a lot of time drawing. I wasn't very good, but I enjoyed it. Actually, I also liked playing video games. My parents thought it was a waste of time, but I loved them.
questions.sampleBand7: I particularly enjoyed reading when I was younger. I used to get lost in books for hours, especially fantasy novels. I also liked messing around with my friends, building forts and things like that. It was a pretty simple childhood, I guess, but a happy one.
questions.sampleBand8: When I was a child, I particularly loved building things. I had this massive box of Lego, and I would spend hours creating all sorts of weird and wonderful contraptions. I wasn't following any instructions or anything; it was all just pure imagination. I think that's what I enjoyed most about it, the freedom to come up with my own designs. Looking back, it probably helped me develop my problem-solving skills.
questions.sampleBand9: Oh, that's an easy one! I was absolutely obsessed with climbing trees as a child. There was this huge oak tree in our garden, and I'd spend hours up there, lost in my own little world. I’d pretend I was a pirate in the crow's nest or an explorer in the jungle, you know? It was my happy place. I think it really fuelled my imagination and gave me a sense of adventure that has stuck with me ever since. Plus, honestly, the view from the top was pretty spectacular. I definitely have fond memories of those days.
questions.sampleAnswer: As a child, I had a wide range of activities I loved. Building things was a particular passion—I spent countless hours constructing elaborate structures with LEGO, creating imaginary cities and vehicles. I was also an avid reader, especially of adventure and fantasy stories that transported me to other worlds entirely. Outdoor play was a big part of my childhood too—cycling around the neighbourhood, playing cricket in the street with friends, and exploring any patch of open land we could find. I also enjoyed drawing and making things by hand—maps of imaginary places, comic strips, simple models. Looking back, most of what I enjoyed as a child involved either creating something or exploring something, which I think reflects personality traits that have stayed with me into adulthood.

questions.uzSampleBand6: Bolaligimda men ko'p vaqtimni chizishga sarflardim. Unchalik yaxshi chiza olmasdim, lekin menga yoqardi. Aslida, video o'yinlar o'ynash ham yoqardi. Ota-onam buni vaqtni behuda sarflash deb hisoblardi, lekin men ularni yaxshi ko'rardim.

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd like to describe the Hagia Sophia in Istanbul, Turkey, which I visited a few years ago and which left a profound and lasting impression on me.

The Hagia Sophia is a monumental structure located in the heart of Istanbul's historic district. It was originally built as a Christian cathedral in 537 AD under the Byzantine Emperor Justinian I, making it nearly fifteen hundred years old. Over its long history, it has served as a cathedral, a mosque, a museum, and most recently, since 2020, it has been reconverted into an active mosque.

In terms of its appearance, the Hagia Sophia is extraordinary. From the outside, it presents a massive central dome flanked by semi-domes and four slender minarets added during the Ottoman period. The scale is immediately impressive—the dome rises approximately 56 metres above the floor and spans 31 metres in diameter. What makes it architecturally remarkable is that when it was built, it was the largest cathedral in the world and remained so for nearly a thousand years. The engineering achievement it represents is staggering given the technology available in the sixth century.

The interior is even more breathtaking than the exterior. When you step inside, the sheer volume of the space is overwhelming—the dome seems to float above you, supported by a ring of windows that flood the interior with natural light, creating an almost ethereal atmosphere. The walls are covered in intricate Byzantine mosaics depicting Christ, the Virgin Mary, and various emperors, alongside Islamic calligraphy and geometric patterns added during the Ottoman era. The layering of these two great artistic and religious traditions within a single space is visually and historically fascinating.

As for what I learned there, the visit was genuinely educational on multiple levels. I learned about Byzantine architecture and the engineering innovations that made the dome possible—including the use of pendentives, which are curved triangular sections that allow a circular dome to sit atop a square base. I also gained a deeper understanding of the complex history of Istanbul itself—a city that has been the capital of the Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman empires, and which carries the traces of all these civilisations in its architecture. The Hagia Sophia embodies this layered history more vividly than almost any other building I've encountered.

Perhaps most importantly, the visit prompted me to reflect on the relationship between architecture, religion, and political power. The building has been claimed and reclaimed by different faiths and empires over the centuries, each leaving their mark while also preserving what came before. This speaks to something profound about how great buildings outlast the ideologies that created them and become shared heritage for all of humanity.

Overall, visiting the Hagia Sophia was one of the most intellectually and aesthetically stimulating experiences I've had while travelling. It's a building that rewards careful attention—the more you look, the more you see, and the more you understand about the extraordinary sweep of human history it represents.

Ayasofya Istanbulning tarixiy markazida joylashgan ulkan inshootdir. U dastlab 537-yilda Vizantiya imperatori Yustinian I davrida xristian sobori sifatida qurilgan bo'lib, uni deyarli bir ming besh yuz yillik qiladi. Uzoq tarixi davomida u sobor, masjid, muzey vazifasini o'tagan va yaqinda, 2020-yildan beri faol masjidga aylantirilgan.

Ko'rinishi jihatidan Ayasofya g'ayrioddiy. Tashqi tomondan u yarim gumbazlar va Usmonlilar davrida qo'shilgan to'rtta ingichka minoralar bilan o'ralgan ulkan markaziy gumbazni namoyish etadi. Ko'lami darhol hayratlanarli - gumbaz poldan taxminan 56 metr balandlikda ko'tariladi va diametri 31 metrni tashkil qiladi. Uni arxitektura jihatidan e'tiborga molik qiladigan narsa shundaki, u qurilgan paytda dunyodagi eng katta sobor edi va deyarli ming yil davomida shunday bo'lib qoldi. Ichki qismi tashqi ko'rinishidan ham hayratlanarliroq. Ichkariga qadam qo'yganingizda, makonning hajmi juda katta - gumbaz sizning ustingizda suzayotgandek tuyuladi, u tabiiy yorug'lik bilan ichki qismni to'ldiradigan derazalar halqasi bilan qo'llab-quvvatlanadi va deyarli efir atmosferasini yaratadi. Devorlar murakkab Vizantiya mozaikalari bilan qoplangan bo'lib, ular Xristos, Bokira Maryam va turli imperatorlarni, shuningdek, Usmonlilar davrida qo'shilgan islom xattotligi va geometrik naqshlarni tasvirlaydi. Ushbu ikkita buyuk badiiy va diniy an'analarning bitta makonda qatlamlanishi vizual va tarixiy jihatdan hayratlanarli.

U yerda nimani o'rganganimga kelsak, tashrif ko'p jihatdan haqiqatan ham ma'rifiy edi. Men, shuningdek, Istanbulning murakkab tarixi haqida chuqurroq tushunchaga ega bo'ldim - Rim, Vizantiya va Usmonli imperiyalarining poytaxti bo'lgan va o'z arxitekturasida barcha ushbu sivilizatsiyalarning izlarini olib yuradigan shahar. Ayasofya ushbu qatlamli tarixni men duch kelgan deyarli har qanday binodan ko'ra yorqinroq aks ettiradi.

Ehtimol, eng muhimi, tashrif meni arxitektura, din va siyosiy hokimiyat o'rtasidagi munosabatlar haqida o'ylashga undadi. Bino asrlar davomida turli e'tiqodlar va imperiyalar tomonidan da'vo qilingan va qayta da'vo qilingan, ularning har biri o'z izini qoldirgan, shu bilan birga oldin kelgan narsani saqlab qolgan. Bu buyuk binolar ularni yaratgan mafkuralardan ustun turishi va butun insoniyat uchun umumiy merosga aylanishi haqida chuqur narsani anglatadi.

Umuman olganda, Ayasofyaga tashrif buyurish sayohat paytida boshimdan kechirgan eng intellektual va estetik jihatdan rag'batlantiruvchi tajribalardan biri edi. Bu diqqat bilan qarashga arziydigan bino - qancha ko'p qarasangiz, shuncha ko'p ko'rasiz va u aks ettirgan insoniyat tarixining g'ayrioddiy ko'lami haqida shunchalik ko'p tushunasiz.

Historic buildings also make history tangible and emotionally resonant in a way that abstract historical accounts rarely achieve. Standing in a space that has witnessed centuries of human activity creates a powerful sense of connection to the past that can inspire curiosity, empathy, and a deeper appreciation of human achievement.

questions.sampleAnswer: This is a nuanced question with legitimate arguments on both sides. In favour of entry fees, charging visitors can generate revenue that funds the conservation and maintenance of scenic spots, which is particularly important for fragile natural environments or historic sites that require ongoing investment to preserve. There's also a philosophical argument that natural landscapes belong to everyone and shouldn't be commodified. A middle-ground approach—free or subsidised access for residents and low-income visitors, with fees for international tourists or premium experiences—may be the most equitable solution.

questions.sampleAnswer: Scenic spots are certainly a popular and often rewarding choice for travellers, but whether they're the 'best' choice depends entirely on what a person hopes to gain from travel. For those seeking natural beauty, a sense of awe, and connection with the physical world, visiting scenic spots can be deeply fulfilling and memorable. However, travel offers many other valuable experiences that scenic spots alone can't provide. Immersing yourself in local culture—visiting markets, attending community events, eating at local restaurants, interacting with residents—can offer insights into a place that no scenic viewpoint can match. Urban exploration, historical sites, and cultural institutions like museums and galleries provide different but equally enriching forms of engagement. The most meaningful travel experiences often combine scenic beauty with cultural depth, human connection, and genuine curiosity about how people live. So rather than prescribing scenic spots as the best choice, I'd argue that the best travel is intentional and varied, drawing on whatever a destination has to offer.

Tabiiy go'zallikni, hayrat tuyg'usini va jismoniy dunyo bilan aloqani his qilishni istaganlar uchun go'zal joylarga tashrif buyurish juda mazmunli va unutilmas bo'lishi mumkin. Biroq, sayohat go'zal joylar yolg'iz o'zi ta'minlay olmaydigan boshqa ko'plab qimmatli tajribalarni taqdim etadi. O'zingizni mahalliy madaniyatga singdirish - bozorlarga tashrif buyurish, jamoat tadbirlarida qatnashish, mahalliy restoranlarda ovqatlanish, aholi bilan muloqot qilish - hech qanday go'zal manzaralar mos kelmaydigan joy haqida tushuncha berishi mumkin. Shahar tadqiqoti, tarixiy joylar va muzeylar va galereyalar kabi madaniy muassasalar turli xil, ammo bir xilda boyituvchi mashg'ulotlarni ta'minlaydi. Eng mazmunli sayohat tajribalari ko'pincha go'zal go'zallikni madaniy chuqurlik, insoniy aloqa va odamlarning qanday yashashi haqidagi chinakam qiziqish bilan birlashtiradi. Shunday ekan, go'zal joylarni eng yaxshi tanlov sifatida belgilashdan ko'ra, men eng yaxshi sayohat maqsadli va xilma-xil bo'lib, yo'nalishning nima taklif qila olishiga asoslanadi, deb aytgan bo'lardim.

questions.prompt: Why do some people like to live in big cities?

Furthermore, the sheer density of cultural amenities – from world-class museums to cutting-edge restaurants – creates an unparalleled lifestyle. Beyond that, some people simply thrive on the energy and anonymity of urban environments, finding a sense of belonging amidst the bustling crowds. questions.sampleAnswer: Big cities offer a concentration of opportunities and experiences that smaller towns and rural areas simply cannot match, which explains their enduring appeal. Economically, cities are where the most diverse and well-paying jobs tend to be concentrated, particularly in sectors like finance, technology, media, and the creative industries. For career-oriented individuals, proximity to major employers, professional networks, and industry events is a significant draw. Culturally, cities offer an extraordinary range of entertainment, dining, arts, and social experiences—world-class museums, restaurants representing cuisines from every corner of the globe, live music, theatre, and festivals. This variety appeals particularly to people who value stimulation and novelty. Cities also tend to have better infrastructure—public transport, healthcare, education, and connectivity—which makes daily life more convenient. For young people especially, the social density of cities—the sheer number of people to meet and connect with—is a powerful attraction. Finally, many people are drawn to the energy and dynamism of urban life, the sense that things are happening and that you're at the centre of them.

questions.uzSampleAnswer: Katta shaharlar shunchaki kichik shaharlar va qishloq joylar taqdim eta olmaydigan imkoniyatlar va tajribalarning jamlanmasini taklif qiladi, bu ularning doimiy jozibasini tushuntiradi. Nihoyat, ko'p odamlar shahar hayotining energiyasi va dinamikasiga, narsalar sodir bo'layotgani va siz ularning markazida ekanligingiz hissi bilan jalb qilinadi.

questions.prompt: Is it necessary for tourists to visit landmarks when travelling in a place?

vocabulary.title: Q14 - Visiting Landmarks
sentenceStarters: I don't think it's strictly necessary...

So, I wouldn't say it's absolutely necessary, but it can certainly enhance the experience for some.

For some, seeing famous landmarks is a key part of the experience; it's almost like a pilgrimage to witness these iconic structures firsthand. However, others might prioritise getting under the skin of a place, exploring local neighbourhoods, trying the cuisine, and really immersing themselves in the culture. So, while landmarks are undoubtedly important, they're not the be-all and end-all of travel.

For some, those iconic sites represent a tangible link to history and culture, and experiencing them firsthand is a powerful draw. They might feel they're missing out on a core aspect of the destination if they don't. Conversely, a growing number of travellers are seeking more authentic and immersive experiences, preferring to venture off the well-trodden path and engage with local communities. Ultimately, I believe the most rewarding travel experiences are those that align with individual interests and preferences, whether that involves ticking off famous landmarks or digging deeper into the local fabric. To each their own, really.
questions.sampleAnswer: I don't think it's strictly necessary, though landmarks are popular for good reasons. Famous landmarks typically represent a place's most significant historical, cultural, or architectural achievements, and visiting them can provide valuable context and a shared reference point for understanding a destination. There's also a social dimension—landmarks are part of a collective cultural vocabulary, and having visited them allows you to participate in conversations and comparisons with other travellers. However, an exclusive focus on landmarks can actually limit the depth of a travel experience. Landmarks are often crowded, commercialised, and experienced in a superficial way—a quick photograph and then moving on. Some of the most memorable travel experiences come from wandering without a fixed itinerary, discovering neighbourhood cafés, talking to locals, or stumbling upon a beautiful but entirely unheralded street or building. The ideal approach is probably a balance: visit the significant landmarks to gain context, but leave plenty of time for unscripted exploration.

questions.prompt: Which do most people prefer, living in a bungalow or in a tall building?

vocabulary.title: Q15 - Bungalow vs Tall Building
idioms: home is where the heart is

questions.sampleAnswer: Preferences vary significantly based on lifestyle, life stage, and cultural context, but I think there are discernible patterns. Bungalows—single-storey houses with gardens—tend to appeal to families with children, older people, and those who prioritise space, privacy, and a connection to outdoor areas. The ability to have a garden, the absence of stairs, and the sense of owning a defined piece of land are significant draws. Tall buildings—apartments or flats in high-rises—tend to appeal more to young urban professionals, singles, and couples without children who prioritise location, convenience, and the amenities of city living over space. The trade-off is typically space and privacy for location and lifestyle access. In many rapidly urbanising countries, the choice is also heavily influenced by economics—land scarcity in cities makes bungalows prohibitively expensive, pushing more people into high-rise living regardless of preference. Culturally, preferences also differ—in some East Asian cities, high-rise apartment living is the norm and carries no stigma, while in many Western countries, the detached house with a garden remains the aspirational ideal.

Tez urbanizatsiya bo'layotgan ko'plab mamlakatlarda tanlovga iqtisodiyot ham katta ta'sir ko'rsatadi - shaharlarda yerning kamligi bungalovlarni haddan tashqari qimmatga tushiradi va ko'proq odamlarni afzalliklaridan qat'i nazar, ko'p qavatli uylarda yashashga majbur qiladi. questions.prompt: How important is it to preserve natural beauty as cities continue to expand?

vocabulary.title: Q16 - Preserving Natural Beauty Amid Urban Expansion
sentenceStarters: Preserving natural beauty is of paramount importance...
As urban areas expand, they often encroach on...

questions.sampleBand5: I think it's important. Cities have many buildings and people need nature too. Without nature, cities are not nice. We should keep parks and trees. People feel happy when they see green.
questions.sampleBand6: I think it's quite important. Many cities are growing too fast and they're cutting down trees. People need green spaces to relax, and animals need places to live. questions.sampleBand7: It's incredibly important, in my opinion. As cities expand, they often consume natural land, which leads to environmental damage and the loss of green spaces. People in cities need contact with nature for their mental health and quality of life. I think governments should make sure urban development includes parks, green corridors and protected zones. Cities like Singapore have shown you can have a modern city and still preserve a lot of natural beauty if you plan well.
questions.sampleBand8: Preserving natural beauty during urban expansion is, undoubtedly, of paramount importance. Cities tend to grow at the expense of forests, wetlands and biodiversity, which not only damages ecosystems but also diminishes residents' well-being. Numerous studies have demonstrated that access to green spaces reduces stress and improves overall health. Beyond that, natural beauty contributes to a city's character and economic value through tourism. Sustainable urban planning—incorporating parks, green roofs, and protected reserves—is the key to balancing growth with preservation.
questions.sampleBand9: Preserving natural beauty as cities expand is, in my view, absolutely crucial—not just for aesthetic reasons but for ecological, psychological, and economic ones. Unchecked urbanisation tends to encroach on forests, wetlands, and coastal zones, leading to habitat destruction and the disruption of ecosystems that regulate air, water and climate. From a human standpoint, green spaces have been consistently shown to enhance mental well-being and foster community cohesion. Cities like Singapore and Vienna prove that high density and natural beauty are not mutually exclusive—through careful planning, green corridors, and vertical gardens, urbanisation and nature can coexist. The real challenge for policymakers is to strike a balance that allows cities to thrive without compromising the environments that ultimately sustain them.
questions.sampleAnswer: Preserving natural beauty as cities expand is, in my view, of paramount importance—not merely for aesthetic reasons but for ecological, psychological, and economic ones. As urban areas grow, they often encroach on forests, wetlands, and coastal zones, leading to habitat destruction and a sharp loss of biodiversity. From a human standpoint, green spaces have been consistently shown to improve mental well-being, reduce stress, and foster a sense of community. Cities like Singapore and Vienna demonstrate that high density and natural beauty are not mutually exclusive—through careful planning, green corridors, and protected reserves, urbanisation and nature can coexist. Economically, preserving natural assets also boosts tourism and raises property values. So while expansion is often inevitable in growing economies, doing so without safeguarding natural environments is short-sighted. The real challenge for policymakers is to strike a sustainable balance that allows cities to thrive without compromising the ecosystems that ultimately sustain them.

questions.sampleBand5: Architecture is important for cities. Buildings show how the city looks. Some cities have famous buildings like Paris has Eiffel Tower. People remember cities by their buildings.
questions.sampleBand6: I think architecture is very important for a city's identity. When you think of a city, you usually think of its famous buildings. For example, Paris has the Eiffel Tower and London has Big Ben. Old buildings also show the history of the city, and new buildings show how modern it is. So buildings tell the story of a place.
questions.sampleBand7: Architecture plays a really important role in shaping a city's identity. The buildings—both old and new—say a lot about the culture, history, and ambitions of a place. Iconic landmarks like the Sydney Opera House or the Eiffel Tower become symbols that the whole world recognises. But it's not just the famous ones; even ordinary streets and traditional houses give a city its character. When cities lose their old buildings, they often lose part of their soul too.
questions.sampleBand8: Architecture, undoubtedly, plays a central role in shaping a city's identity. It functions as the enduring expression of a place's history, values, and aspirations. Iconic landmarks often become synonymous with the cities they inhabit, while vernacular architecture reflects local climate, materials, and cultural traditions. When historic buildings are sacrificed to careless redevelopment, cities risk losing the very character that distinguishes them. Conversely, thoughtful integration of modern design with the historic fabric produces cities with layered identities that stand the test of time.
questions.sampleBand9: Architecture plays a profoundly important role in shaping a city's identity—it is, in many ways, the most visible and enduring expression of that identity. The skyline, the layout of streets, the materials, and the fusion of old and new all contribute to how a city is perceived. Iconic landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower or the Sydney Opera House become cultural symbols that convey a city's values and aspirations to the world. Beyond famous landmarks, vernacular architecture—traditional houses, religious buildings, and public spaces—reflects the climate, materials, and cultural traditions of a place, giving each city its distinctive character. When a city loses its soul to careless redevelopment, something irreplaceable is sacrificed. Conversely, cities that thoughtfully integrate modern architecture with their historic fabric develop richer, more layered identities that honour both past and future.
questions.sampleAnswer: Architecture plays a profound role in shaping a city's identity—it is, in many ways, the most visible and enduring expression of that identity. The skyline, the layout of streets, the materials used, the fusion of old and new—all of these contribute to how a city is perceived both by its residents and by visitors. Iconic buildings often become synonymous with the cities they inhabit: the Eiffel Tower for Paris, the Sydney Opera House for Sydney, or Burj Khalifa for Dubai. These landmarks are not just structures; they are cultural symbols that convey values, aspirations, and history. Beyond famous landmarks, vernacular architecture—the traditional houses, religious buildings, and public spaces—reflects the climate, materials, and cultural traditions of a place, giving each city its distinctive character. When a city loses its architectural heritage to careless redevelopment, it often loses something of its soul too. Conversely, cities that thoughtfully integrate modern architecture with their historic fabric tend to develop richer, more layered identities that honour both their past and their future.
questions.uzSampleBand5: Arxitektura shaharlar uchun muhim. Binolar shaharning qanday ko'rinishini ko'rsatadi. Ba'zi shaharlarda mashhur binolar bor — masalan, Parijda Eyfel minorasi. Odamlar shaharlarni ularning binolari orqali eslab qolishadi.

Shunday qilib, binolar joyning hikoyasini aytib beradi.
questions.uzSampleBand7: Arxitektura shaharning o'ziga xosligini shakllantirishda haqiqatan ham muhim rol o'ynaydi. Binolar — eski ham, yangi ham — joyning madaniyati, tarixi va orzulari haqida ko'p narsani aytib beradi. Sidney opera teatri yoki Eyfel minorasi kabi mashhur diqqatga sazovor joylar butun dunyo tan oladigan ramzlarga aylanadi. Lekin faqat mashhur binolar emas; oddiy ko'chalar va an'anaviy uylar ham shaharga o'ziga xos xarakter beradi. Shaharlar eski binolarini yo'qotganda, ko'pincha jonlarining bir qismini ham yo'qotishadi.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Arxitektura, shubhasiz, shaharning o'ziga xosligini shakllantirishda markaziy rol o'ynaydi. U joyning tarixi, qadriyatlari va orzularining doimiy ifodasi sifatida xizmat qiladi. Mashhur diqqatga sazovor joylar ko'pincha o'zlari joylashgan shaharlar bilan bir ma'noli bo'lib qoladi, vernakulyar arxitektura esa mahalliy iqlim, materiallar va madaniy an'analarni aks ettiradi. Tarixiy binolar e'tiborsiz qayta qurishga qurbon qilinganda, shaharlar o'zlarini farqlovchi xarakterni yo'qotish xavfi ostida qoladi. Aksincha, zamonaviy dizaynni tarixiy to'qima bilan o'ylab birlashtirish vaqt sinovidan o'tadigan ko'p qatlamli o'ziga xoslikka ega shaharlarni yaratadi.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Arxitektura shaharning o'ziga xosligini shakllantirishda g'oyat muhim rol o'ynaydi — u ko'p jihatdan o'sha o'ziga xoslikning eng ko'rinadigan va doimiy ifodasidir. Osmono'par chiziq, ko'chalar tartibi, materiallar va eski va yangining uyg'unligi shahar qanday qabul qilinishiga hissa qo'shadi. Eyfel minorasi yoki Sidney opera teatri kabi mashhur diqqatga sazovor joylar dunyoga shaharning qadriyatlari va orzularini yetkazib beruvchi madaniy ramzlarga aylanadi. Mashhur landmarklardan tashqari, vernakulyar arxitektura — an'anaviy uylar, diniy binolar va jamoat joylari — joyning iqlimi va madaniy an'analarini aks ettiradi va har bir shaharga o'ziga xos xarakter beradi. Shahar e'tiborsiz qayta qurish tufayli jonini yo'qotsa, qaytarilmas narsa qurbon qilinadi. Aksincha, zamonaviy arxitekturani tarixiy to'qima bilan o'ylab birlashtirgan shaharlar o'tmish va kelajakni hurmat qiladigan boyroq, ko'p qatlamli o'ziga xoslikni rivojlantirishadi.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Arxitektura shaharning o'ziga xosligini shakllantirishda chuqur rol o'ynaydi — u ko'p jihatdan o'sha o'ziga xoslikning eng ko'rinadigan va doimiy ifodasidir. Osmono'par chiziq, ko'chalar tartibi, ishlatiladigan materiallar, eski va yangining uyg'unligi — bularning barchasi shaharning aholisi va mehmonlari tomonidan qanday qabul qilinishiga hissa qo'shadi. Mashhur binolar ko'pincha shaharlar bilan bir ma'noli bo'lib qoladi: Parij uchun Eyfel minorasi, Sidney uchun Sidney opera teatri yoki Dubay uchun Burj Khalifa. Bu mo'jaz binolar shunchaki inshootlar emas; ular qadriyatlar, intilishlar va tarixni anglatuvchi madaniy belgilardir. Mashhur diqqatga sazovor joylardan tashqari, vernakulyar arxitektura — an'anaviy uylar, diniy binolar va jamoat joylari — joyning iqlimi, materiallari va madaniy an'analarini aks ettiradi va har bir shaharga o'ziga xos xarakter beradi. Shahar e'tiborsiz qayta qurish tufayli o'zining arxitektura merosini yo'qotsa, ko'pincha jonidan ham bir narsani yo'qotadi. Aksincha, zamonaviy arxitekturani tarixiy to'qima bilan o'ylab birlashtirgan shaharlar boyroq, ko'p qatlamli o'ziga xoslikni rivojlantirishga moyil.
